title: ergonomic stream handles, credential cascade, and cross-language compatibility
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Multiple SDK customers and internal examples reveal ergonomic gaps when consumers need to implement long-lived streaming interactions while coordinating credential refresh/fallback logic. This PR introduces a small, idiomatic SessionHandle abstraction across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs and a credential-cascade strategy that lets SDKs transparently try delegated credentials, cached tokens, then fallback to a configured static token.

Summary of changes: introduced SessionHandle in each SDK to centralize heartbeat/keepalive, cancelation, and resume hints; added a CredentialCascade manager that accepts an ordered list of credential providers (delegated, cached, static) and exposes a single GetToken() surface; harmonized streaming types so cross-language integration tests exercise identical behavior; bump Python/TS/Go SDK versions to signal the ergonomic changes; and added migration notes and examples in each SDK docs folder.

Checklist: [x] implement SessionHandle in Python/TS/Go; [x] implement CredentialCascade with fallback and metrics; [x] add unit tests for fallback ordering; [x] add crosslang integration tests exercising resume and reauth; [x] docs and changelogs updated; [ ] coordinate rollout with product for non-backwards-breaking feature flag.

Compatibility notes: The change is additive — existing call sites still work. Consumers that relied on the previous ad-hoc token rotation should opt into CredentialCascade via a boolean flag in SDK config to get automatic fallthrough behavior. SessionHandle introduces a small typed object returned from start_stream() in each SDK; backward compatibility shims are provided (old start_stream() still returns an iterator/async generator when shimmed).

Testing and CI: packaged cross-language integration test harness that spins up a local token-mock and a minimal echo server, exercising token expiry and fallback behavior. One flaky integration test was isolated and stabilized (see CI notes).

Related work: Linear ENG-7812 (session ergonomics), ENG-7813 (credential cascade), and customer support SUP-3312 (incidence summary).

review_comments: Marco Li: Nice API — please add explicit docstring on SessionHandle.close() semantics (synchronous vs async) in Python so users don't accidentally leak sockets.
Aisha Patel: Added docstring and updated examples to show recommended usage patterns. Also added a close_many utility to close multiple handles concurrently.
Sofia Gómez: CredentialCascade looks good. Request: expose a metrics tag for 'fallthrough.reason' so ops can alert on abnormal fallback frequency.
Aisha Patel: metrics tag added, and unit tests updated to assert the tag is emitted on each fallback path.
Evan Carter: integration test flaked once on CI due to port contention in the harness — patched harness to pick ephemeral ports.
release_notes: SDKs: Introduced SessionHandle for ergonomic long-lived streams, added CredentialCascade for ordered credential fallback (delegated -> cached -> static). Backwards compatible; users can opt-in via SDK config. Version bumps: python 1.28.0, typescript 2.3.0, go 1.5.0.
